insights.title: Mortgages are the riskiest AND the biggest book
insights.finding: Mortgages default at 24.7% vs 16.1% portfolio average, and hold 52% of total exposure.
insights.so_what: Secured loans should be safer. Review mortgage underwriting first: this is where most of the money is at risk.

insights.title: Default falls steadily as income rises
insights.finding: Lowest income band defaults at 24.6%, highest at 9.7%.
insights.so_what: Income is the strongest single driver. Use loan-to-income limits, and verify income more strictly for the lowest band.

insights.title: Age matters a lot; region barely matters
insights.finding: Under-30s default at 21.6% vs 6.8% for 60+. Regions only range 15.0%-16.9%.
insights.so_what: Focus risk rules on borrower profile, not geography. Regional pricing would add little.

insights.title: Unemployed borrowers are a very high-risk group
insights.finding: Unemployed borrowers default at 35.0%, 2.2x the portfolio average.
insights.so_what: Require proof of other income or collateral before lending to this group.

insights.title: Cross-cut: income x employment
insights.finding: Low-income contract workers default at 27.6%, but only 12.0% one band up. Unemployed borrowers stay at 20.0% even in the top income band.
insights.so_what: For contract workers, income is the key check. For the unemployed, high stated income does not remove the risk.
